calibration_guidance: Use the full numeric range. Do not assign mid-high scores by default just because an idea is plausible. A total score above 85 should mean the idea is clearly strong across importance, novelty, definition, execution, conceptual simplicity, and breadth of applicability. A total score above 90 should be rare. Prefer one coherent idea nucleus whose technical machinery serves a single consequential claim over a bundle of independently publishable aims. Do not confuse simplicity with brevity or under-specification, and do not penalize complexity essential to define or validate the core result. A simple idea that is already known remains low-novelty; simplicity and generality never substitute for novelty evidence. A merely reasonable idea with unclear novelty or weak execution plan should usually fall around 55-75, not 80+.

marks.label: Intent Relevance
marks.guidance: Score alignment with the core user intent, including the target domain, central constraint, and practical research goal. Do not require one idea to absorb every optional extension or requested observable. 10: directly targets the core scientific intent. 7: mostly matches, with only minor drift. 4: relevant but misses an important constraint or payoff. 2: weak topical overlap. 0: wrong problem or domain.

marks.label: Novelty
marks.guidance: Score how publishable the idea would be if worked out successfully, not the evidence that it is new. 15: confidently publishable in a top journal of the field. 10: marginally publishable in a top journal, or clearly publishable in a strong field journal. 5: marginally publishable in a second-tier or specialized journal if executed well. 0: not publishable as research even if completed. Do not give extra marks for ideas beyond top-journal novelty; overly creative ideas are not more useful for the current agent workflow.

marks.label: Confidence
marks.guidance: Score only the evidence that this work has not already been done, not how good the idea is. Search the internet and, when available, ARC paper tools before assigning this mark; do not rely only on memory. 15: targeted ARC/web search found no close prior work and the idea looks genuinely unclaimed. 10: no direct prior work found, but nearby literature is dense or the search was incomplete. 5: significant risk it has been done; close related work exists and the distinction is not yet secure. 0: search finds the same or essentially equivalent work already done. If runtime restrictions prevent new searches, use the supplied search evidence and state the limitation.

marks.label: Value
marks.guidance: Score whether a leading researcher in this research domain should read the resulting paper if the idea is worked out. 15: must-read for leading researchers in the domain. 10: good-to-know; useful contribution but not field-shaping. 5: modest niche value or mostly incremental clarification. 0: even if correct, the result would not be worth reading.

marks.label: Planning
marks.guidance: Score whether the question is broken into good-enough pieces for agent execution. Do not award extra marks for adding separable observables, formalisms, or future extensions. 10: concrete, agent-executable steps with clear inputs, outputs, and validation checks. 7: clear route, though some details remain. 4: some steps are too broad or difficult for an AI agent. 0: most steps cannot be done by an AI agent or the plan is essentially absent.

marks.label: Well-definedness
marks.guidance: Score whether the question is set up sharply enough. 15: problem is sharply specified; the calculation can be set up directly from the proposal. 10: mostly well-defined, but requires a few reasonable choices or assumptions. 5: interesting direction, but key objects, setup, limits, or observables are under-specified. 0: no clear calculable question.

marks.label: Simplicity
marks.guidance: Use scientific taste to score conceptual economy and unity, not prose length. 10: one nontrivial idea nucleus with minimal assumptions; every major calculation and method is essential to that core claim. 7: a clear core with limited, justified supporting machinery. 4: a worthwhile core is obscured by avoidable choices or separable goals. 0: novelty is manufactured by stacking loosely connected ideas, observables, or methods. Necessary technical controls, validation, and mathematical detail do not reduce this score.

marks.label: Generality
marks.guidance: Score breadth of applicability and robustness under relaxing special assumptions. 10: the core result applies, or has a controlled route to apply, across a broad physically meaningful class of cases with few special choices. 7: it covers a natural family beyond one benchmark. 4: it is tied to a narrow setup but reveals a principle that may transfer. 0: it is a tuning-specific or benchmark-specific artifact with no credible wider use. Do not reward vague lists of future applications, parameter scans, or extra observables. Broader applicability can make future experimental verification more likely, but direct observability is not a separate requirement.

total_score.label: Total
total_score.guidance: Set total_score to the closest integer after summing all listed marks. Rank ideas by total_score on one common scale.
